meta.title: Thai Alphabet
meta.subtitle: 92 letters, vowels, tone marks and digits · both directions, as two cards each
meta.desc: The Thai script: 92 notes, in the order a Thai primer teaches it — the 44 consonants in their traditional order, the vowels, the four tone marks and three other signs, the three consonant classes that decide a syllable's tone, and the ten Thai digits. The first deck of the Thai collection. Both directions: see a letter and recall its sound, or see a sound and recall the letter, each a card with its own schedule. Every consonant is given with its NAME — Thai letters are named by a word that starts with them (ก ไก่, g as in chicken) — and the name is how Thais tell apart the letters that sound alike, so the sound side names it too: five letters say k and six say t. Each consonant shows its CLASS, mid, high or low, which together with the tone marks decides the tone of every syllable, and its sound at the start and at the end of a syllable (บ is b at the start and p at the end). Each vowel is written on ◌, the dotted circle standing for the consonant it sits on, since a Thai vowel can be written above, below, before or after its consonant. Every sound is given in the Paiboon romanisation the level decks use — bp and dt for the unaspirated p and t of spin and stop — and described in English words, with one everyday word that shows it and a speaker beside the letter and the word. The sounds are approximations, as every learner's alphabet gives them. Sources: the standard description of Central Thai; the example words' romanisations are English Wiktionary's, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0).

fields.Name: ก ไก่
fields.Sound:
gɔɔ gài · “chicken”mid class
k with no puff of breath, as in skin; Paiboon writes it g; at the end of a syllable: k

fields.Name: ข ไข่
fields.Sound:
kɔ̌ɔ kài · “egg”high class
k with a puff of breath, as in kit; at the end of a syllable: k

fields.Name: ฃ ขวด
fields.Sound:
kɔ̌ɔ kùuat · “bottle”high class
k with a puff of breath — OBSOLETE, still recited in the alphabet

fields.Name: ค ควาย
fields.Sound:
kɔɔ kwaai · “water buffalo”low class
k with a puff of breath, as in kit; at the end of a syllable: k
fields.Example: ควายkwaaiwater buffalo

fields.Name: ฅ คน
fields.Sound:
kɔɔ kon · “person”low class
k with a puff of breath — OBSOLETE, still recited in the alphabet

fields.Name: ฆ ระฆัง
fields.Sound:
kɔɔ rá-kang · “bell”low class
k with a puff of breath, in words from Sanskrit and Pali; at the end of a syllable: k

fields.Name: ง งู
fields.Sound:
ngɔɔ nguu · “snake”low class
ng as in sing — and Thai lets it START a word; at the end of a syllable: ng

fields.Name: จ จาน
fields.Sound:
jɔɔ jaan · “plate”mid class

fields.Name: ฉ ฉิ่ง
fields.Sound:
chɔ̌ɔ chìng · “small cymbals”high class
ch as in chip, with a puff of breath; never ends a syllable
fields.Example: ฉิ่งchìngsmall cymbals

fields.Name: ช ช้าง
fields.Sound:
chɔɔ cháang · “elephant”low class
ch as in chip, with a puff of breath; at the end of a syllable: t

fields.Name: ซ โซ่
fields.Sound:
sɔɔ sôo · “chain”low class
s as in sun; at the end of a syllable: t

fields.Name: ฌ เฌอ
fields.Sound:
chɔɔ chəə · “tree, wood”low class
ch as in chip; rare, in words from Sanskrit and Pali

fields.Name: ญ หญิง
fields.Sound:
yɔɔ yǐng · “woman”low class
y as in yes; at the end of a syllable: n

fields.Name: ฎ ชฎา
fields.Sound:
dɔɔ chá-daa · “headdress”mid class
d as in dog; rare, in words from Sanskrit and Pali; at the end of a syllable: t

fields.Name: ฏ ปฏัก
fields.Sound:
dtɔɔ bpà-dtàk · “goad”mid class
t with no puff of breath, as in stop; rare, in words from Sanskrit and Pali; at the end of a syllable: t

fields.Name: ฐ ฐาน
fields.Sound:
tɔ̌ɔ tǎan · “base, pedestal”high class
t with a puff of breath, as in top; rare, in words from Sanskrit and Pali; at the end of a syllable: t

fields.Name: ฑ มณโฑ
fields.Sound:
tɔɔ mon-too · “Montho, a queen of the Ramakien”low class
t with a puff of breath, sometimes d; rare, in words from Sanskrit and Pali; at the end of a syllable: t

fields.Sound:
nɔɔ neen · “novice monk”low class
n as in no; in words from Sanskrit and Pali; at the end of a syllable: n

fields.Name: ด เด็ก

dɔɔ dèk · “child”mid class
d as in dog; at the end of a syllable: t

fields.Name: ต เต่า

dtɔɔ dtào · “turtle”mid class
t with no puff of breath, as in stop; Paiboon writes it dt; at the end of a syllable: t

fields.Name: ถ ถุง
fields.Sound:
tɔ̌ɔ tǔng · “bag”high class
t with a puff of breath, as in top; at the end of a syllable: t

fields.Name: ท ทหาร
fields.Sound:
tɔɔ tá-hǎan · “soldier”low class
t with a puff of breath, as in top; at the end of a syllable: t

fields.Name: ธ ธง
fields.Sound:
tɔɔ tong · “flag”low class
t with a puff of breath, as in top; in words from Sanskrit and Pali; at the end of a syllable: t

fields.Name: น หนู
fields.Sound:
nɔɔ nǔu · “mouse”low class
n as in no; at the end of a syllable: n

fields.Name: บ ใบไม้
fields.Sound:
bɔɔ bai-máai · “leaf”mid class
b as in bat; at the end of a syllable: p

fields.Name: ป ปลา
fields.Sound:
bpɔɔ bplaa · “fish”mid class
p with no puff of breath, as in spin; Paiboon writes it bp; at the end of a syllable: p

fields.Name: ผ ผึ้ง
fields.Sound:
pɔ̌ɔ pʉ̂ng · “bee”high class
p with a puff of breath, as in pin; never ends a syllable

fields.Name: ฝ ฝา
fields.Sound:
fɔ̌ɔ fǎa · “lid”high class
f as in fan; never ends a syllable

fields.Name: พ พาน
fields.Sound:
pɔɔ paan · “offering tray”low class
p with a puff of breath, as in pin; at the end of a syllable: p

fields.Name: ฟ ฟัน
fields.Sound:
fɔɔ fan · “tooth”low class
f as in fan; at the end of a syllable: p

fields.Name: ภ สำเภา
fields.Sound:
pɔɔ sǎm-pao · “junk (sailing ship)”low class
p with a puff of breath, as in pin; in words from Sanskrit and Pali; at the end of a syllable: p

fields.Name: ม ม้า
fields.Sound:
mɔɔ máa · “horse”low class
m as in man; at the end of a syllable: m

fields.Name: ย ยักษ์

yɔɔ yák · “giant”low class
y as in yes; at the end of a syllable: i (it closes the vowel, as in ai)

fields.Name: ร เรือ

rɔɔ rʉʉa · “boat”low class
a tapped or trilled r — in casual speech often said as l; at the end of a syllable: n

fields.Name: ล ลิง

lɔɔ ling · “monkey”low class
l as in leaf; at the end of a syllable: n

fields.Name: ว แหวน
fields.Sound:
wɔɔ wɛ̌ɛn · “ring”low class
w as in wet; at the end of a syllable: o (it closes the vowel, as in ao)

fields.Name: ศ ศาลา
fields.Sound:
sɔ̌ɔ sǎa-laa · “pavilion”high class
s as in sun; in words from Sanskrit and Pali; at the end of a syllable: t

fields.Name: ษ ฤๅษี
fields.Sound:
sɔ̌ɔ rʉʉ-sǐi · “hermit”high class
s as in sun; in words from Sanskrit and Pali; at the end of a syllable: t

fields.Name: ส เสือ
fields.Sound:
sɔ̌ɔ sʉ̌ʉa · “tiger”high class
s as in sun; at the end of a syllable: t

fields.Name: ห หีบ
fields.Sound:
hɔ̌ɔ hìip · “chest, box”high class
h as in hat; written silent before a low-class letter (หนู, หญิง) to give it the high class's tones; never ends a syllable

fields.Name: ฬ จุฬา
fields.Sound:
lɔɔ jù-laa · “star kite”low class
l as in leaf; rare, in words from Sanskrit and Pali; at the end of a syllable: n
fields.Example: จุฬาjù-laastar kite

fields.Name: อ อ่าง
fields.Sound:
ɔɔ àang · “basin”mid class
no sound of its own: it carries a vowel that begins a syllable, and is a vowel itself (ɔɔ) after a consonant

fields.Name: ฮ นกฮูก
fields.Sound:
hɔɔ nók-hûuk · “owl”low class
h as in hat; never ends a syllable

fields.Name: สระอะ
fields.Sound: a · short a, as in the u of cut

fields.Name: สระอา
fields.Sound: aa · long a, as in father

fields.Name: สระอิ
fields.Sound: i · short i, as in bit

fields.Name: สระอี
fields.Sound: ii · long ee, as in see

fields.Name: สระอึ
fields.Sound: ʉ · short ʉ: say i as in bit with the lips spread and the tongue pulled back; English has no such vowel

fields.Name: สระอือ
fields.Sound: ʉʉ · long ʉʉ, the same unrounded vowel held; written ◌ื with อ when no consonant follows

fields.Name: สระอุ
fields.Sound: u · short u, as in put; written BELOW the consonant

fields.Name: สระอู
fields.Sound: uu · long oo, as in food; written below the consonant

fields.Name: สระเอะ
fields.Sound: e · short e, as in bed; เ is written BEFORE the consonant it follows in speech

fields.Name: สระเอ
fields.Sound: ee · long e, like the a of cake held without the glide into ee

fields.Name: สระแอะ
fields.Sound: ɛ · short ɛ, as in the a of cat, clipped

fields.Name: สระแอ
fields.Sound: ɛɛ · long ɛɛ, as in the a of cat, held

fields.Name: สระโอะ
fields.Sound: o · short o, like the o of go cut short, with no glide

fields.Name: สระโอ
fields.Sound: oo · long o, as in go held without the glide into oo

fields.Name: สระเอาะ
fields.Sound: ɔ · short ɔ, as in the o of hot

fields.Name: สระออ
fields.Sound: ɔɔ · long ɔɔ, as in law

fields.Name: สระเออะ
fields.Sound: ə · short ə, as in the u of fur, clipped
fields.Example: เยอะyə́a lot

fields.Name: สระเออ
fields.Sound: əə · long əə, as in fur with no r

fields.Name: สระเอีย
fields.Sound: iia · ee gliding into a, as in the ia of Mia
fields.Example: เสียงsǐiangsound, voice

fields.Name: สระเอือ
fields.Sound: ʉʉa · the unrounded ʉʉ gliding into a

fields.Name: สระอัว
fields.Sound: uua · oo gliding into a, as in the ua of truant

fields.Name: สระอำ
fields.Sound: am · short a followed by m, as in the um of hum

fields.Name: สระใอไม้ม้วน
fields.Sound: ai · ai, as in Thai; this spelling (mái múan) is used in only twenty words, which primers learn by heart

fields.Name: สระไอไม้มลาย
fields.Sound: ai · ai, as in Thai; the usual spelling (mái má-laai)

fields.Name: สระเอา
fields.Sound: ao · ao, as in the ow of cow

fields.Name: ไม้หันอากาศ
fields.Sound: a · mái hǎn-aa-gàat: short a, written this way when a final consonant follows (กัน = g + a + n)

fields.Name: ไม้ไต่คู้
fields.Sound: (short) · mái dtài-kúu: SHORTENS the vowel of the syllable it sits on (เป็น is bpen, not bpeen)
fields.Example: เป็นbpento be

fields.Name: ฤ
fields.Sound: rʉ · a vowel letter from Sanskrit, said rʉ (sometimes ri or rəə)

fields.Name: ไม้เอก
fields.Sound: mái èek · tone mark 1: LOW tone on a mid- or high-class consonant (ไก่ gài), FALLING on a low-class one (ไม่ mâi)

fields.Name: ไม้โท
fields.Sound: mái too · tone mark 2: FALLING tone on a mid- or high-class consonant (บ้าน bâan), HIGH on a low-class one (ม้า máa)

fields.Name: ไม้ตรี
fields.Sound: mái dtrii · tone mark 3: HIGH tone; written only on mid-class consonants

fields.Name: ไม้จัตวา
fields.Sound: mái jàt-dtà-waa · tone mark 4: RISING tone; written only on mid-class consonants
fields.Example: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวgǔai-dtǐaonoodles
fields.Word: ก๋วยเตี๋ยว

fields.Name: การันต์
fields.Sound: gaa-ran · the silencer (thanthakhat): the letter under it is not pronounced — ศุกร์ is sùk, the ร silent
fields.Example: ศุกร์sùkFriday (in วันศุกร์)

fields.Name: ไม้ยมก
fields.Sound: mái yá-mók · the repeat mark: say the word before it twice

fields.Name: ไปยาลน้อย
fields.Sound: bpai-yaan-nɔ́ɔi · the abbreviation mark: the rest of a long name is left out (กรุงเทพฯ for the city's full ceremonial name)
fields.Example: กรุงเทพฯgrung-têepBangkok

fields.Name: อักษรกลาง
fields.Sound: MID class, the nine letters ก จ ฎ ฏ ด ต บ ป อ: with no tone mark, a live syllable is MID tone and a dead one LOW; they alone take all four tone marks. A syllable is LIVE when it ends in a long vowel or in m, n, ng, w or y, and DEAD when it ends in a short vowel or in p, t or k.

fields.Name: อักษรสูง
fields.Sound: HIGH class, the eleven letters ข ฃ ฉ ฐ ถ ผ ฝ ศ ษ ส ห: with no tone mark, a live syllable is RISING tone and a dead one LOW. A syllable is LIVE when it ends in a long vowel or in m, n, ng, w or y, and DEAD when it ends in a short vowel or in p, t or k.

fields.Name: อักษรต่ำ
fields.Sound: LOW class, the other twenty-four: with no tone mark, a live syllable is MID tone; a dead one is HIGH if its vowel is short and FALLING if it is long. A syllable is LIVE when it ends in a long vowel or in m, n, ng, w or y, and DEAD when it ends in a short vowel or in p, t or k.
